questions.prompt: Walk through astraboot1's content chain from ContentItem to the owner's active release: what role does each link play, how is the immutability of a published version actually enforced (and against whom), how does a new release go live, and why does all of this matter for a learner's past attempts?

keyPoints.text: ContentItem is only the identity: it says the exercise exists.
keyPoints.quote: `ContentItem` is the identity ("this exercise exists").

keyPoints.text: ContentVersion holds an immutable payload plus checksum, unique per (itemId, version); a change is a new version, never an edit.
keyPoints.quote: Published content is never edited — a change is a new version.

keyPoints.text: ReleaseItem maps a published release to the exact versions it contains.
keyPoints.quote: `ReleaseItem` maps a published release to the exact versions it contains.

keyPoints.text: The owner's activeReleaseId switches transactionally with publication, so no half-live release is ever visible.
keyPoints.quote: there is no instant where half the new release is live.

keyPoints.text: Immutability is a database trigger, not a convention: any UPDATE or DELETE on a content version raises an error.
keyPoints.quote: Immutability is not a convention here — it's a trigger.

keyPoints.text: Because the rule lives in the database, it binds every writer that issues an UPDATE or DELETE (a future bug, a migration script, a psql session), not just the TypeScript code path.
keyPoints.quote: even from a future bug, a migration script, or a psql session.

keyPoints.text: Attempts and review events point at exact versions, so what you answered stays the thing you actually answered.
keyPoints.quote: what you answered is forever the thing you actually answered.

keyPoints.text: Editing content in place would silently rewrite the meaning of every past attempt.
keyPoints.quote: the alternative (editing content in place) silently rewrites the meaning of every past attempt.

questions.prompt: How does astraboot1 use revisions for optimistic concurrency? Name which records carry a revision, what a write must present, what happens (server and client) on a mismatch, and how prior draft sources are retained and pruned.

keyPoints.text: ExerciseDraft, Note, ReviewState and MissionProgress carry integer revisions (LessonProgress has a similar version counter).
keyPoints.quote: `ExerciseDraft`, `Note`, `ReviewState` and `MissionProgress` carry integer revisions

keyPoints.text: A write presents the revision it read.
keyPoints.quote: A write presents the revision it read

keyPoints.text: A mismatch is a 409 REVISION_CONFLICT, meaning the record changed on another device.
keyPoints.quote: a 409 `REVISION_CONFLICT` ("changed on another device")

keyPoints.text: On that conflict the client keeps its draft rather than losing it.
keyPoints.quote: the client keeps its draft

keyPoints.text: DraftSnapshot keeps the twenty prior draft sources, pruned in the same transaction as the write that adds the twenty-first.
keyPoints.quote: `DraftSnapshot` retains the twenty prior draft sources (pruned in the same transaction as the write that adds the twenty-first).

questions.prompt: Which rules does astraboot1 make the database own, how does it decide whether a rule belongs in the database, in Zod at the route boundary, or both, and what are its retention and backup arrangements (including what the JSON export is not)?

keyPoints.text: Foreign keys enforce every relational reference.
keyPoints.quote: Foreign keys enforce every relational reference.

keyPoints.text: CHECK constraints bound note and source lengths and review steps, and require positive versions and XP.
keyPoints.quote: SQL `CHECK` constraints bound note and source lengths, review steps, and require positive versions and XP.

keyPoints.text: Anything that must be true regardless of which code path writes belongs in the database: uniqueness, immutability, bounds.
keyPoints.quote: anything that must be true *regardless of which code path writes* belongs in the database — uniqueness, immutability, bounds

keyPoints.text: Rules that need a friendly message are also validated in Zod at the route boundary.
keyPoints.quote: anything that needs a friendly message is also validated in Zod at the route boundary.

keyPoints.text: The same rule in both places is intentional defense in depth, not duplication.
keyPoints.quote: that's intentional defense in depth, not duplication.

keyPoints.text: Learning history and mutation receipts are kept indefinitely; maintenance prunes only expired or revoked sessions.
keyPoints.quote: Maintenance currently prunes expired/revoked sessions only.

keyPoints.text: Backups are pg_dump with a separately tested restore; the JSON export is a user-facing copy, not the backup strategy.
keyPoints.quote: the JSON export in `personal.ts` is a user-facing data copy, not the backup strategy.
